items.question:
An actuarial operations head at a life insurer has run a Claude-assisted workflow for drafting actuarial assumption documentation for eighteen months. The workflow saves time on initial drafts but auditors have noted that assumption justifications frequently require significant rework during the annual reserve review — more so than before Claude was adopted. The chief actuary and head of internal audit are both expressing concern.

Which TWO actions are MOST appropriate given this evidence? (Choose TWO)

options.A: Continue the workflow but add a senior actuary review step before any assumption documentation enters the audit process, accepting the rework cost as a quality control measure.
options.B: Expand the workflow to cover more actuarial documentation types so that the time savings across a larger scope justify the rework cost in assumption justifications.
options.C: Suspend the workflow for assumption justification documentation pending a root-cause review that includes the auditors and senior actuaries whose concerns are on record.
options.D: Conduct a structured post-mortem examining whether the observed rework increase is attributable to the AI workflow or to other factors (reviewer changes, assumption complexity increases, updated audit standards) that coincided with deployment.
options.E: Present the time savings data to the chief actuary as evidence that the programme is net positive despite the rework increase, and request more time before any structural decision.

items.question:
An executive director at a youth development NGO wants her three programme officers to use Claude consistently for drafting volunteer appreciation notes, programme update newsletters, and partnership renewal letters. Each officer currently drafts these differently, and the ED spends time editing them to align voice and structure before distribution.

What is the MOST efficient way to reduce the ED's editing burden while preserving each officer's ability to personalise the content?

options.A: Build a separate prompt template for each of the three document types, each specifying the required structure, voice, and key message elements, and share them with all three programme officers as the starting point for each draft.
options.B: Ask the programme officers to route all drafts through the ED for approval before distribution, ensuring quality control remains centralised.
options.C: Train the three programme officers on advanced prompting techniques over a two-day workshop so they can independently develop their own consistent prompt approaches.
options.D: Create a single universal Claude prompt covering all three document types and ask officers to specify which document they need at the start of each session.
